blocks.source: Vol III, Long-Term Memory, § Historical Perspective and Further Reading
blocks.md: Long before digital computers possessed the capacity to store vast text collections, researchers recognized that locating the right record among many is a selection problem rather than a storage problem. In his influential vision of the memex, @bush1945memex imagined a desk-sized device that would house an individual's books, records, and correspondence, allowing the user to establish associative trails between related items. Bush observed that human memory operates by association rather than formal indexing, and he located the primary engineering difficulty in selection rather than physical storage capacity.

questions.q: The section **Historical Perspective and Further Reading** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A session must observe its own committed memory writes on later reads, which a lagging index or replica silently violates unless reads are pinned to a generation at or after the write.

The runtime, not the model, decides what persists: admission checks run before deduplication, same-scope updates supersede by compare-and-swap, and deletion (on request, on withdrawn consent, or at the end of a recorded retention period) is a lifecycle event the store must honor.

The unit of evaluation is the whole memory policy run through isolated multi-session trials with lifecycle fixtures, scored by task acceptance and cost per accepted task including background maintenance.

Every read is a bounded request answered by an envelope that reports scope, snapshot, completeness status, and per-item provenance, and an empty result proves nonexistence only for a complete search of the declared scope.
